motion.name: list-reflow
motion.purpose: Coordinated row and panel reflow, 24px/97% entry and 12px edit feedback in each direction; movement is disabled with reduced motion.

motion.name: list-exit
motion.purpose: Confirmed completion and deletion fade and move 24px right at 97% scale. Reduced motion uses a stationary 160ms fade.

motion.name: list-highlight
motion.purpose: Primary tint marks confirmed additions, edits and reopened items. New changes extend the feedback window; reduced-motion fades use 160ms.

motion.name: pending-spinner
motion.purpose: The pending checkbox and suggestion use the existing spinner utility. Reduced motion keeps a static loading glyph with aria-busy.

motion.name: list-finale
motion.purpose: Off-by-default final pointer completion uses three confetti waves with a 240ms banner entry and 160ms exit. Reduced motion shows a stationary check and heading for 1600ms with 160ms fades.

motion.name: list-finale-check
motion.purpose: Left-to-right clip reveal of the green finale check. Reduced motion displays the complete check immediately.

motion.name: list-finale-heading
motion.purpose: The heading fades and settles from 15% below at 95% scale; reduced motion keeps it stationary.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Occasional surfaces and pointer feedback retain fades; other CSS motion is capped at .01ms and smooth scrolling is disabled.

narrative.overview:
Liquid Glass inspired controls float over a readable household board. Cool pearl ground, white work surfaces and blue actions keep the light theme crisp; midnight ground and pale blue actions carry the same hierarchy in dark mode. A softly illuminated rim and restrained shadow distinguish navigation from the content underneath.

The interface retains aligned rows and opaque reading surfaces. Independent settings groups use separate cards with icon headings; related content rows can use dividers within their shared surface. Apple system typography leads the existing font stack, with self-hosted Public Sans as the fallback. Density changes with the available space; touch actions, readable labels and explicit states remain visible.
keyCharacteristics: Pearl and midnight grounds with blue actions.
Glass navigation, header controls and transient menus over opaque content.
System typography, rounded capsules and a clear reading hierarchy.
Responsive density, generous portrait touch controls and solid accessibility fallbacks.

rules.name: Meaning Before Color
rules.body: Pair selected, offline, loading, error and completion colors with text, icons or semantic state; color is never the only cue.

rules.name: Read Before Decoration
rules.body: Use the existing sentence-case heading hierarchy and concise action labels. Give content the strongest typographic emphasis.

rules.name: Glass Control Layer
rules.body: Reserve glass for the main dock, header controls and transient menus, popovers and dialogs, with one local exception: calendar timetable frames reuse the shared panel glass on School, dashboard previews and the expanded view. Keep the regular calendar, lists, form fields and other recurring work panels opaque; saved image/PDF timetables retain their existing presentation.

rules.name: Settings Grouping
rules.body: Give each independent settings or customization group an opaque card and a meaningful heading icon. Keep related fields together, preserve visible heading text and separate cards with space instead of relying on divider lines.

dos: Do reuse semantic CSS colors so the dark theme follows the same roles.
Do keep the portrait reading scale and large list, event and navigation targets.
Do preserve visible focus, text wrapping, scrollable overflow and safe-area clearance.
Do provide solid surfaces for reduced transparency, increased contrast and unavailable backdrop filtering.
Do show unavailable, pending and empty states distinctly.
Do keep examples fictional and household data outside committed design assets.
donts: Don't shrink or hide task content to force a tall screen into one viewport.
Don't encode a person, device state or selected route through color alone.
Don't spread glass beyond the documented control layers and calendar timetable and Smart home card exceptions, or add decorative gradients or elevation to other recurring work panels.
Don't turn a timetable preview into a cropped substitute for the full, pageable view.
Don't describe CSS blur and specular edges as native optical refraction.
